subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: Statement: Some pens are books. Which conclusion definitely follows?
formula: Some A are B ⇒ Some B are A
explain: A particular affirmative converts simply: Some B are A.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: Statement: No cat is a rat. Which definitely follows?
formula: No A is B ⇒ No B is A
explain: A universal negative converts simply: No B is A.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: All pens are books. All books are cups. Which definitely follows?
formula: All A are B, All B are C ⇒ All A are C
explain: Two universal affirmatives give a universal affirmative.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: All kings are men. No man is a bird. Which definitely follows?
formula: All A are B, No B is C ⇒ No A is C
options: Some men are kings and birds
explain: All A are B, No B is C gives No A is C.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: Some tables are chairs. All chairs are woods. Which definitely follows?
formula: Some A are B, All B are C ⇒ Some A are C
explain: Particular + universal affirmative gives a particular affirmative.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: Some A are B. No B is C. Which definitely follows?
formula: Some A are B, No B is C ⇒ Some A are not C
explain: Particular + universal negative gives a particular negative.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: A conclusion based on outside general knowledge, not the statement, is...
options: Following if true in real life
explain: Only information given in the statement may be used.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: Statement: Only graduates are eligible for the post. Which definitely follows?
formula: Only A are B ⇒ All B are A
options: Every eligible person is a graduate
All graduates will get the post
explain: 'Only A are B' means every B is an A.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: Statement: Some books are not novels. Which definitely follows?
explain: 'Some A are not B' means not all A are B; it has no simple converse.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: Some A are B. Some B are C. All C are D. Which definitely follows?
formula: Some B are C, All C are D ⇒ Some B are D
explain: Only the pair B–C–D links: Some B are D. A–B is only partial.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: Neither of two conclusions follows alone. Which pair makes 'Either I or II' follow?
formula: Contradictory pair (same terms)
options: Some A are B / No A is B
All A are B / No A is B
All A are B / All B are A
Some A are B / Some B are A
explain: Either-or needs a complementary pair; one is always true.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: In statement–assumption questions, an implicit assumption is best described as:
options: Something taken for granted but left unstated
A fact explicitly mentioned in the statement
A conclusion drawn from the statement
A course of action suggested by it
explain: An implicit assumption is an unstated idea the speaker takes as true when making the statement.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: Statement: 'Wear a helmet while riding.' Which is the implicit assumption?
options: Helmets reduce the risk of head injury
Every rider meets with an accident
Riding is banned without a helmet
explain: The advice only makes sense if helmets protect the head.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: 'Ban plastic bags to curb pollution.' Which is implicit in this statement?
options: People will never use plastic again
explain: The ban is meant to curb pollution, so plastic bags must be assumed to add to it.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: 'Fuel prices have been raised to curb consumption.' Implicit assumption?
explain: The measure works only if higher price reduces consumption.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: Notice: 'Do not litter. Fine ₹500.' Which is implicit?
options: The fine will deter people from littering
explain: A fine is imposed assuming the fear of penalty deters the act.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: 'Read the manual before operating the machine.' Implicit assumption?
options: The manual gives useful operating guidance
explain: The advice is meaningful only if the manual helps in correct operation.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: A valid implicit assumption must be:
options: Necessary for the statement to hold
explain: It must be a needed background link, not just a compatible or repeated idea.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: 'Send it by speed post so that it reaches by Monday.' Implicit assumption?
options: Speed post is faster than ordinary post
Speed post is free of cost
explain: Choosing speed post for timely arrival assumes it is faster.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: Teacher: 'Submit by Friday, else marks will be deducted.' Implicit assumption?
explain: The threat works only if students value their marks.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: 'Dial 100 in case of an emergency.' Which is implicit?
options: Help is available through that number
Only police can help in emergencies
explain: The advice assumes calling 100 will bring a response.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: 'Our hotel is 5 minutes from the airport. Book now!' Implicit assumption?
options: Travellers prefer hotels close to the airport
All other hotels are far away
explain: The proximity claim attracts customers only if they value nearness to the airport.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: 'Use LED bulbs to cut electricity bills.' Which is the implicit assumption?
options: Everyone will switch to LED bulbs
LED bulbs consume less power than ordinary bulbs
Electricity bills are going to rise soon
LED bulbs are cheaper than all other bulbs
explain: Advice to cut bills works only if LEDs use less power; the others are extra or absolute claims.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: Should smoking be banned in public places? Pick the STRONG argument.
options: Yes, it harms the health of non-smokers
No, it has been allowed for decades
explain: Strong arguments are factual, important and directly relevant to the issue.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: An argument that only rephrases the statement, e.g. 'Yes, because it should be done', is:
options: Strong if the statement is true
explain: Restating the claim gives no reason, so it is circular and weak.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: An argument built on one personal example or an isolated case is generally judged:
options: Strong if the case is recent
explain: One instance cannot justify a general policy, so the argument is weak.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: 'Yes, because several other nations have already done it' is usually treated as:
options: Strong if the nations are developed
explain: Imitation is not a reason; it does not address merit or local conditions.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: A true fact that has no bearing on the question asked makes an argument:
options: Strong, if it is widely known
explain: An argument must be relevant to the statement; truth alone is not enough.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: Should the retirement age be raised? Pick the STRONG argument.
options: No, it has never been changed
Yes, life expectancy and fitness have increased
No, my uncle retired happily at 60
explain: It gives a relevant, general, factual reason; the others are personal, vague or traditional.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: An argument that uses 'always', 'never' or 'all' with no support is typically:
options: Strong if it is a 'Yes' argument
explain: Sweeping generalisations without evidence are weak arguments.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: 'Yes, because the Prime Minister has said so' is judged as:
options: Strong if the PM is an expert
explain: Mere reliance on a person's say-so gives no reason on merit.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: 'No, because it has never been done before' is a typical example of a:
options: Strong if the tradition is old
explain: Appeal to tradition or precedent is not a valid reason, so it is weak.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: Statement: A lake is polluted by factory waste. Which course of action is most suitable?
options: Shut all factories in the country permanently
Make factories treat waste before discharge
explain: Treating waste at source is practical and proportionate; the others are drastic or irrelevant.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: Statement: Many students of a school failed in Maths. Which course of action follows?
explain: Remedial classes address the weakness directly; the others avoid or worsen the problem.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: Statement: The cause of repeated fires in a factory is unknown. Which course is most apt?
options: Order an inquiry into the cause
Close every factory in the state
explain: When the cause is unknown, a probe into it is the logical and practical first step.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: Statement: A bridge has been found structurally unsafe. Which course of action follows?
options: Close it to traffic until repaired
Raise the toll on the bridge
Demolish all bridges in the city
explain: Stopping use until repair protects lives and is proportionate to the problem.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: Statement: Heavy rain may flood riverside villages. Which course of action follows?
options: Shift villagers to safe places in advance
explain: Timely evacuation is a practical preventive step against the predicted danger.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: Statement: Pulse prices have risen sharply. Which course of action is most suitable?
options: Release buffer stock into the market
explain: Releasing buffer stock increases supply and eases prices; the others are irrelevant or harmful.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: Statement: A clerk was found negligent in his duties. Which course of action is most suitable?
options: Issue him a warning or show-cause notice
explain: A proportionate, corrective step targets only the negligent person; the others are extreme or illogical.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: Statement: Dengue cases are rising in a city ward. Which course of action is most apt?
options: Shut down every hospital for cleaning
Begin fogging and clear stagnant water
Ban all outdoor activities in the city
explain: A practical, proportionate step that tackles the cause (mosquito breeding); others are extreme or irrelevant.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: Rohan wore a 'lucky' shirt and then won. Concluding 'the shirt caused the win' is which flaw?
formula: Post hoc ergo propter hoc
explain: Coming after an event in time does not make something its cause.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: Water is necessary for plant growth. A plant has water. Conclusion: it will surely grow. This:
formula: Necessary ≠ sufficient
explain: Water is a necessary condition, not a sufficient one; other factors are also needed.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: Fit people exercise daily. Concluding 'fitness makes people exercise' instead of the reverse is called:
explain: Reverse causation means mistaking the effect for the cause.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: 'The delay was mostly due to traffic.' Conclusion: Traffic was the only cause. This:
formula: mostly ≠ only
explain: 'Mostly' allows other minor causes, so 'only' is too strong.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: Ice-cream sales and drowning cases both rise in summer. Conclusion: ice cream causes drowning. The flaw is:
explain: Both effects arise from a third factor, summer heat; correlation is not causation.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: If it rains, the road gets wet. The road is wet. Conclusion: It rained. This:
options: Follows only if the road is old
explain: Affirming the effect is invalid; the road may be wet from other causes.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: If the power fails, the lights go off. The lights are on. Conclusion: The power did not fail. This:
formula: If P → Q, then not Q → not P
explain: Absence of the effect rules out a sufficient cause (contrapositive).

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: Statement: Smoking causes lung disease. Conclusion: Every smoker will get lung disease. This:
options: Is the reverse of the statement
explain: A cause raises the risk or likelihood; it does not guarantee the effect in every case.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: Statements: No A is B; All B are C. Which follows?
formula: E + A → O (Some C are not A)
explain: The B's are C but not A, so some C are not A. No A is C is not forced.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: Statements: No A is B; No B is C. Which follows?
formula: E + E → no conclusion
explain: Two negative premises never give a definite conclusion.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: Statements: Some A are B; Some B are C. Which follows?
formula: I + I → no conclusion
explain: Two particular premises give no definite conclusion.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: Statements: All A are B; All C are B. Which follows?
formula: Undistributed middle (B is predicate twice)
explain: B is the predicate of both premises, so it is undistributed; nothing definite follows.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: If "All A are B" is true, what is the valid converse?
formula: A → I (conversion by limitation)
explain: A-type converts to I-type: Some B are A.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: Which statement is the contradictory (opposite) of "All A are B"?
formula: A ↔ O and E ↔ I are contradictories
explain: A and O are contradictories: they cannot both be true or both be false.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: Statements: All A are B; All B are C. Which conclusion follows?
formula: A + A → A, and A converts to I
explain: All A are C converts to Some C are A. All C are A is not forced.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: Which pair of conclusions on the same terms is complementary (either-or)?
formula: A–O contradictory pair
options: All S are P; Some S are not P
No S is P; Some S are not P
All S are P; No S is P
Some S are P; Some S are not P
explain: All and Some-not contradict each other: exactly one must hold, so they form an either-or pair.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: All A are B; All B are C. Which is a possibility?
explain: A ⊂ B ⊂ C, and C can be larger than A. The others contradict the chain.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: Given: All A are B; Some B are C. Which is a possibility?
explain: Some A may lie within the B that are C; the others contradict a given statement.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: Which test shows that a statement is a necessary assumption of an argument?
formula: Negation test
options: It is a widely known fact
Its negation makes the conclusion collapse
explain: If denying the assumption destroys the conclusion, the assumption is necessary.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: Drug X cured mice, so it will cure humans. Which most weakens this?
options: Humans lack the enzyme through which X acts
X was tested on many mice
Mice are cheap to use in labs
explain: In an argument by analogy, a relevant difference between the cases weakens it.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: 90% of 50 people surveyed like the new park, so most citizens like it. Which weakens this?
options: The survey took only one day
explain: An unrepresentative sample weakens a generalisation from it.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: Argument: Roads widened, so accidents will fall. Which statement most strengthens this?
options: Accidents occurred on narrow roads earlier
Wider roads in similar towns saw fewer accidents
Roads were widened at great cost
explain: Evidence from comparable cases linking the cause to the effect supports the causal claim.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: Which type of statement strengthens an argument by removing a rival explanation of the evidence?
options: One that questions the evidence given
One that adds an unrelated fact
One that rules out an alternative cause
explain: Ruling out alternative causes makes the stated cause more likely, so it strengthens a causal argument.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: Statement: "Only a few students passed the test." Which conclusion follows?
explain: "Only a few" means a small number passed, so the rest failed.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: Statement: "Smokers may develop lung disease." Which conclusion follows?
options: Every smoker will get lung disease
Smokers can never avoid lung disease
Lung disease is possible in smokers
explain: "May" signals possibility; "will", "never" and "only" overstate it.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: Statement: "Few employees got a bonus." Which conclusion follows?
explain: "Few" means a small number, but at least some, got it.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: Statement: "Most roads in the city are damaged." Which conclusion follows?
formula: Most ⇒ Some
explain: "Most" includes "some", but never "all" or "none".

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: Statement: Some A are B. Conclusion: Some A are not B. This conclusion:
options: Follows only if all B are A
explain: 'Some A are B' leaves open that all A are B, so 'some A are not B' is only a possibility.

subject: Logical Reasoning
prompt: Given 'All A are B', which of these is a valid possibility?
explain: A and B may coincide (same set), so 'All B are A' is possible.
